candidate.title: Smart-seq / NanoCAGE / CAGEscan
candidate.scope: The assigned grouped Illumina poster row illustrates the SMART template-switching cDNA-preparation component, ending at purified DNA. Its poly(A)/oligo(dT) material route is represented literally for original Smart-seq. NanoCAGE and CAGEscan remain distinct named targets of the grouped row: each has a separate, primary-supported local template-switching interface below, beginning with random-primed first-strand cDNA. Those interfaces resolve member applicability; they are not additional branches drawn in the poster, and are not connected to the fixed oligo(dT)-derived Smart-seq intermediates. The shared component does not establish identical complete library preparations. Adjacent Quartz-Seq, DP-Seq and Smart-seq2 rows and the right-hand chemical structure are outside scope; none is an alternative within this row.

operations.description: Copies the depicted poly(A)-tailed RNA into first-strand cDNA from the adapter-bearing oligo(dT) primer, producing the RNA:cDNA intermediate with a terminal CCC extension.

method_scopes.rationale: The grouped row names NanoCAGE, a distinct method rather than an alias of Smart-seq or CAGEscan. The Plessy et al. implementation uses random-primed RT and preferential 5′ cap capture by template switching; the shared mechanism is represented by this separate local interface. None of the four fixed-history oligo(dT)-derived Smart-seq operations is reassigned to NanoCAGE, including downstream PCR and Purify. The primary method also uses semi-suppressive PCR and ultimately produces short DNA tags representing RNA 5′ ends, supporting capped-end/promoter-usage profiling. Tag generation and library-specific processing are not depicted in this row and are not added as operations. This component-level inclusion does not claim that the poster specifies its full NanoCAGE library. Capped-end capture alone does not distinguish primary transcription initiation from secondary capping.
